solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With six-footer outside, add his Cockney muscle (10)

indicators.note: the ANT sits outside the rest, wrapping it

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a Cockney's muscles with a tall man standing by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' looks like a tall person; it is an insect with six feet. An antagonist is a muscle that works against another.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is a muscle whose action opposes that of another muscle.

clue.text: Sharp card player follows playing king (6)

indicators.note: E comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: East, one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A shrewd card player sits down after a king has been played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing king' reads as a card game; AS is the 'playing' of an actor's role, and the king is an Egyptian one. Bridge players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means sharp-witted, shrewd.

clue.text: Pair of timid aquatic birds with no name flap (6)

indicators.note: take the first two letters
birds 'with no name' literally lack the letter standing for name, so N comes out of SWANS

explanation.surface: Two nervous water birds flap about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like something wings do; here it is a noun, a state of panic. Tiswas is British slang for a state of confusion or agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in British slang: 'all of a tiswas' and 'in a flap' both describe a state of flustered panic.

clue.text: Sucker on steep drinks, a feature of Cornwall (9,5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, GOON sits on top of the rest

blocks.note: a goon = a fool, a dupe
to down = to drink in one

explanation.surface: A sucker drinks heavily on a steep slope, a scene from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like a verb for soaking; it is the adjective. Goonhilly Downs is an area of the Lizard peninsula in Cornwall, known for its satellite earth station.
explanation.definitionFit: Goonhilly Downs is a stretch of upland heath on Cornwall's Lizard peninsula.

clue.text: Disciple’s uplifting time with Paul’s guitar, regularly wanting Yesterday? (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting SON upward reads it backwards
something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at even intervals, every second one

blocks.note: a son = a disciple or follower; the 's = is
even letters of PAULSGUITAR: A, L, G, I, A

explanation.surface: A Beatles fan is lifted by Paul McCartney's guitar and a performance of Yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all Beatles, and 'Yesterday' is the song; in the definition it is the past itself, which nostalgia longs for.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: the feeling means longing for the past, and 'Yesterday' stands for that past while also naming the Beatles song.

clue.text: Tyke heading to Swaledale flock? (5)

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of Swaledale

blocks.note: a camp = a group of like-minded people

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman heads off to the sheep of Swaledale.
explanation.walkthrough: A tyke is also a Yorkshireman, and Swaledale is a Yorkshire valley with its own breed of sheep, so 'flock' looks like sheep. Here a tyke is a cheeky child.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe a cheeky, mischievous child, though tyke also carries the Yorkshireman sense the surface plays on.

clue.text: Maybe mechanic’s assistant runs electronic device (4)

explanation.surface: A mechanic's apprentice operates a piece of electronic kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The assistant looks like a person; it is the ramp a car is driven up so the mechanic can work underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic uses a ramp to raise a car, so it is one of his aids.

clue.text: Vigorous Greek patrols hotel lounge on vacation (8)

indicators.note: ATTIC goes round the other letters, as a guard patrols an area
lounge is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An energetic Greek walks round the hotel lounge while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like a holiday; it is the convention for emptying a word. Attic, capitalised, means Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone physically strong and energetic.

clue.text: Wine now included in lunch? (8)

indicators.note: what is included in something is held within it, so IN sits within POTAGE

blocks.note: potage = thick soup, a lunch for example

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether wine is included with lunch now.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes in right after the P. Pinotage is a red grape and wine from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinotage is a South African red wine.

clue.text: Footwear relative briefly left with Ivy perhaps (7,7)

indicators.note: cut short: BROTHER loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Footwear passed on from a relative who left it with an aunt called Ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant. Brothel creepers are thick crepe-soled suede shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothel creepers are soft-soled shoes popular with Teddy Boys.

clue.text: Shop closed having inserted key (5)

indicators.note: the first word has had the key inserted into it, as a key goes into a lock, so ESC goes inside TO

blocks.note: a door pushed to is closed
the Escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A shop is shut and someone has put a key in the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: The key looks like a door key; it is the one on a keyboard. Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tesco is Britain's biggest supermarket chain, one kind of shop.

clue.text: University dons exploring common echinoderm (3,6)

indicators.note: SEARCHIN' puts on U, wearing it inside
in common speech the final G is dropped

blocks.note: searching, with the G dropped as in common speech

explanation.surface: University dons explore the life of a common sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers; it is the verb 'puts on'. 'Common' marks the dropped G of searchin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: echinoderms are the spiny-skinned sea animals, starfish and urchins among them.

clue.text: Tube drivers swelter, needing rotation (7)

indicators.note: the last letter goes round to the front

blocks.note: the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: London Underground drivers swelter and need a shift rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is the windpipe. RACHEAT with the T moved to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific thing: the windpipe is the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Constant nursing at medical unit for one? (7)

definitions.text: Constant nursing at medical unit for one?

indicators.note: PI holds AT, as one nurses a baby

explanation.surface: Someone receives constant nursing on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a patient, someone nursed in an ENT unit, while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes someone being nursed on an ENT ward, and the question mark flags that this is just one example.

clue.text: Labour article, approaching broadcast, using jargon (12)

indicators.note: said on air, so only the sound counts

explanation.surface: The Labour party's line, approaching a broadcast, is full of jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital L makes 'Labour' look like the British political party; it is plain hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloganeering is using catchphrases and slogans, a kind of jargon.

clue.text: Yank climbing peak managed to consume music (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, BEN goes upward, so reads backwards
what you consume goes inside you, so RAN swallows SKA

blocks.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain

explanation.surface: An American climber eats while listening to music on the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nebraskan is a native of Nebraska, an American, and Yank is informal for any American.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Yank is informal British for any American, and a native of Nebraska is one.

clue.text: Sail away aboard Princess and land near the Gulf (8)

indicators.note: JIB OUT goes inside DI, as on a ship

blocks.note: a jib is a triangular sail

explanation.surface: A princess sails away on a yacht bound for a country near the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sail away' looks like an instruction to leave; the sail is a noun. Djibouti lies on the Gulf of Aden.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is an African country on the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: Self-proclaimed favourite male Russian mostly rash (8)

indicators.note: most of IGOR, losing the last letter

blocks.note: IGOR, a Russian man's name, cut short

explanation.surface: A self-styled favourite Russian man is mostly reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' reads as the adjective, reckless; it is the skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection that shows as a rash.

clue.text: Comic, male, pursues number one rating? (5,7)

indicators.note: BUCK comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: jimmy riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, and number one is a child's word for urinating
a tar is a sailor, as is a rating
a buck is a male deer or rabbit

explanation.surface: A male comedian chases the top rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one rating' suggests top of the charts. Jimmy Tarbuck is a British comedian and TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Tarbuck is a Liverpool-born stand-up comic.

clue.text: Good Alsatian succeeded against fine miniature (6)

indicators.note: S is placed right next to AI

blocks.note: bon is French for good, and Alsace is in France
S = succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A good Alsatian dog wins against a fine miniature breed.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian looks like a dog; it is a person from Alsace, who would say bon for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun used alone: a miniature is anything made small, and the Japanese art grows trees in miniature.

clue.text: Take a fiver off someone? That’s mean (6)

blocks.note: a fiver is a five-pound note; the prefix DE- means removing, so strip someone of a note
the verb: to signify, not the adjective for stingy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether taking a fiver off a person is a mean act.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: taking a note away is to de-note someone. 'Mean' looks like stingy; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the invented DE-NOTE sense (to strip of a banknote) plus the ordinary verb sense, to signify.

clue.text: Brother’s constraining college headwear (7)

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold in check, so BR'S holds ETON within its bounds

explanation.surface: A brother is made to wear his college hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bretons are women's hats with an upturned brim, named after Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: A breton is a hat with a rounded crown and upturned brim.

clue.text: Force half to stop at sign repeatedly (5)

indicators.note: apply 'half' to a word and only its first half survives
do it to each of the next words in turn

explanation.surface: A police force is told to stop at the sign every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' means halve each of stop, at and sign. The Stasi was East Germany's secret police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the state security force of East Germany.

clue.text: In retirement home, no men acknowledge plant (7)

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow
it reads backwards, going back

blocks.note: the letters in homE NO MEN Acknowledge

explanation.surface: In a retirement home with no men, residents acknowledge a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement home' looks like one place; 'retirement' is the reversal sign and 'home' starts the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific thing: the anemone, or windflower, is one of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Standard mixing bowl (5,4)

blocks.note: the jack is the small ball bowled at in the game of bowls

explanation.surface: A standard mixing bowl from the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a kitchen item. 'Standard' is a flag, and the Union Jack is the UK's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a standard is a flag or banner, and the UK's national flag is one.

clue.text: Very quick to ditch Romeo, saucy thing (5)

indicators.note: to ditch a partner is to dump them, so Romeo is dumped out of PRESTO

blocks.note: R in the NATO alphabet; removed

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to dump her Romeo, the cheeky thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy thing' reads as a cheeky person; it is literally a thing that is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition: 'saucy thing' usually means a cheeky person, but here it is literally a thing that is a sauce, the basil one from Genoa.

clue.text: Implement for e.g. rough and smooth? (4)

blocks.note: the rough is the long grass off a golf fairway, and a golfer picks a metal-headed club to play out of it
the verb: to press out creases in clothes

explanation.surface: A tool for both rough and smooth work.
explanation.walkthrough: The rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway, played out of with an iron club; 'rough and smooth' looks like a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club used from the rough, and to iron is to smooth.

clue.text: Champ now private, tense, boxed in US capital (6-4)

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for a noun: 'now is when to champ'

indicators.note: something boxed in is shut inside a container, so DIME is the box around INNER and T

blocks.note: a dime is a US coin; capital = money
inner = private, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A champion, now a private soldier, is tense and confined in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US capital' wants to be Washington; it is money, a dime. 'Champ' is not a winner but the verb to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner-time is when you champ, chewing your food.
